  "text": "Every morning, Mr. Bell opened the station café at six and put two cups beside the kettle.

One was for him. The other had belonged to his daughter, who used to help before school. It said WORLD’S OKAYEST EMPLOYEE in chipped blue letters.

She lived in Canada now. When she called, one of them was always eating the wrong meal.

In November, a young man began waiting outside before opening time. He wore a supermarket uniform beneath his coat.

“You know the first train isn’t till twenty past,” Mr. Bell said.

“I’ve just got off the last bus.”

The young man bought tea and sat near the radiator. Sometimes he slept until the departure board clicked.

On the third morning, Mr. Bell gave him the chipped cup.

“Bigger than the paper ones.”

The young man turned it around and read the words.

“Bit generous.”

His name was Sami. He stacked shelves overnight and attended a training course two towns away. He never explained what the course was, and Mr. Bell kept forgetting to ask.

One Monday, Sami didn’t come. Nor Tuesday.

On Wednesday, Mr. Bell put the second cup back in the cupboard.

At six on Thursday, someone knocked on the glass.

Sami stood outside wearing a shirt and an uncomfortable-looking tie.

“Interview,” he said when the door opened.

Mr. Bell filled the kettle.

“Tea?”

“Please. In the lucky one.”

After Sami left, Mr. Bell washed the cup and dried it carefully. Then he took a photograph of it for his daughter.

Still in use, he wrote.

Her reply arrived during the lunchtime rush.

I should hope so."
